newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly higher on soybean ral.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly higher on soybean ral.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended mostly higher and three-month highs were set amid supply concerns, traders said.
USDA Friday cut estimates for U.S. soybean production and ending stocks and raised usage. Also, traders noted concern that hot, dry conditions in South America would hurt crops.
At the same time, cold weather in the U.S. Midwest was boosting livestock consumption of soymeal.
The January soybean meal contract peaked at $239.00 per ton, the highest level since October 10. January soyoil touched 24.92 per lb, the highest since September 30.
Funds bought at least 3,000 lots soymeal and 4,000 lots soyoil on the day.
Traders said E.D. and F. Man International was a buyer of the March and May soymeal.
Griffin Trading bought 1,000 lots March soyoil and Refco Inc bought 1,000 March, traders said.

Soymeal closed $1.50 lower to $3.10 per ton higher with January up $3.10 at $238.70 and distant deferred months showing some weakness. Soyoil ended 0.14 to 0.20 per lb higher with January up 0.17 at 24.65.
Soymeal volume was estimated at 30,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 39,843 contracts.
Soyoil volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, against Friday's record total of 56,858 contracts.
